NASA remains on track to launch the four Artemis III astronauts in summer 2027 from Kennedy Space Center on a 14-day mission in low-Earth orbit, where they will dock with and test lunar landers engineered by Blue Origin and SpaceX, the agency announced.

Artemis III is considered a key proving-ground mission before NASA sends astronauts to land on the moon's harsh surface during Artemis IV in 2028. The mission will involve interplay between three massive rockets: NASA's Space Launch System, Blue Origin's New Glenn, and SpaceX's Starship.

"We're launching three of the most powerful rockets in the world and undertaking what is likely the most complicated launch campaign ever undertaken," Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, told reporters Friday, Oct. 23, during a news conference at the KSC Press Site.

"Beyond the two docking demonstrations, the crew will conduct Orion systems and crew-survival-suit evaluations, human research, science experiments, and technology demonstrations — validating the coordination of multiple launch systems ahead of future lunar landings," a NASA summary said.
